 Departmental Highlights
 Headcount at DCASE is up two budgeted positions, with an additional position in the Cultural Affairs Coordinator II title and a new Finance Officer title.
 Although the amount is minor, DCASE draws from the corporate fund this year, which it had not in recent previous years: $133,580 from the corporate fund goes towards salary and salary adjustments for the two new titles added in this year’s budget. 
 Outside contracting through the professional and technical services is up dramatically in this year’s DCASE budget, a $4.5 million increase (46.3%). Slightly more than matching that amount, DCASE’s prior year $4.9 million appropriation for delegate agency pass-through funding has been entirely eliminated from the 2027 proposal.
 Historical Context
 After a relatively stable decade of funding, DCASE’s budget underwent several years of dramatic fluctuations during the COVID-19 pandemic. DCASE’s budget initially dropped in 2021 as shutdowns of events and hotels cut off its main source of revenue, then rebounded with pandemic relief funds in 2022, peaking at 2024 and declining in 2025 and 2026. The current proposal would increase the department’s appropriations by 0.8% from the previous year.

 Estimated Fringe Costs 
 City budgets do not break out “fringe” pension and benefit costs for non-grant positions by department, instead grouping them together as citywide expenses under the Finance General section of the budget. To better reflect the real cost of service for departmental operations, BGA Policy has included an estimate of pension and benefit costs for the years 2018-2026, using Department of Finance fringe memos from each relevant year. An estimated fringe cost for the 2027 proposal uses the average annual rate of increase for each of the inputs into the fringe formulae. 
 Based on the city’s fringe formulae, the DCASE fringe cost for nongrant employees averaged 7.2% from 2018-2026, compared to a citywide average of 26.8%. (Departments with a larger proportion of their budget dedicated to non-employee costs or with a larger proportion of grant-funded employees tend to have lower fringe costs, as their pension/benefit costs are either already factored into grant funds or are a smaller percentage of the overall departmental budget.)

 Budgeted Positions & Vacancies 
 Outside of a pandemic-influenced dip in 2021, staffing levels at DCASE have remained relatively stable over the years, unlike the department’s fluctuating appropriations. Overall, the department’s budgeted headcount grew at an average annual rate of 0.3% from 2011-2026, compared to a citywide average annual change of -0.1%. The current proposal would increase budgeted headcount by 2.5% from the previous year.

 Change from Previous Year 
 Outside contracting through the professional and technical services is up dramatically in this year’s DCASE budget, a $4.5 million increase (46.3%). Slightly more than matching that amount, DCASE’s prior year $4.9 million appropriation for delegate agency pass-through funding has been entirely eliminated from the 2027 proposal. 
 Similarly, funding for festival production is up $3 million from the previous year (a 26.7% increase), while grant funds held in reserve balance are down just over $3 million (-40.4%).
